title: Wire the first building option into the reported DOCUMENT (task 1 of 2, ONE PR with task 2; four parts): A the results contract ADDITIVE version 1.4.0 (a new optional building_alternatives list with floor schedules and each building's preliminary capacity estimate, and the by-portion coverage fields; every existing block keeps its shape and benchmark content); B the server (emit the new blocks; footprint figure withheld where the two lot areas disagree; building B conditional; building A absent on the benchmark; legal unit limit stays withheld; name each gap kind); D the register (split the checker, add the DB-211 guards, update + render); E regenerate the committed document and its snapshots and the two server content tests once. Nothing feasible; no human verdict [D-090 R147,R192,R239,R255,R256,R257,R267,R322,R374,R379,R509,R526,R540,R541,R543,R544,R556,R570,R650,R688,R700,R707]
objective: TASK 1 of 2 (reviewed at ONE common head with task 2 and merged as ONE pull request). Connect the four accepted M5-T145 modules to the reported RESULTS DOCUMENT and the register. PART A: extend the contract ADDITIVELY to version 1.4.0, following the 1.1.0/1.2.0/1.3.0 precedent (optional blocks bound by a version allOf; every earlier instance stays valid byte-for-byte; DB-196) - a new optional top-level building_alternatives block (a LIST of worked buildings, each with its floor schedule and its own preliminary capacity estimate, each stating its way and conditions), and the by-portion coverage fields; building_option, unit_estimate, floor_stack, floor_by_floor, max_lot_coverage and geometry KEEP their shape and their benchmark content. PART B: call corner_reach_area (via result_way_bridge), lot_coverage_by_portion, first_building_options and preliminary_apartment_estimate; follow the conflicting-area rule (work order section 6, R257/R239) - the footprint IN SQUARE FEET is shown only where the recorded and outline areas AGREE (compare_lot_area), and WITHHELD where they disagree (benchmark); emit building_alternatives (benchmark: building B alone, conditional on the recorded area; building A absent, it needs the footprint figure); the single building_option block stays not_available with a reason pointing to building_alternatives; name each gap kind (R650); the legal dwelling-unit limit stays withheld; add the DB-212 (d) storey tolerance to first_building_options.py. PART D: update the register (split review_register_calculations.py first, add the DB-211 (a)(b) guards before any six-step verdict moves, update the calc entries' actual sides and render). PART E: regenerate the committed results document, its drawings/CAD snapshots and the two server content tests once. Nothing is called feasible; no human verdict.
business_reason: The four modules are built and reviewed but reachable from no reported result. Task 1 makes the first building option (building B on the benchmark) and the preliminary capacity estimate appear in the results DOCUMENT and the register, in the owner's order, with the conflicting-area and withheld rules kept. An ADDITIVE contract keeps every existing block's shape and benchmark content, so the drawings, CAD, PDF and the web source that read existing blocks do not break; only full-document consumers change, and task 1 and task 2 are reviewed at one head and merged together so the whole CI is green once.
inputs: The four accepted modules (imported; only first_building_options.py changed): corner_reach_area.py (measure_corner_reach_area; CornerPortionAreas), lot_coverage_by_portion.py (permitted_footprint_by_portion), first_building_options.py (building_a/building_b -> FloorSchedule), preliminary_apartment_estimate.py.

The contract precedent: packages/contracts/schemas/v1/results.schema.json - additionalProperties false, contract_version an append-only enum (1.0.0-1.3.0), version-binding allOf; DB-196 (a)-(c) names the homes the new work needs. The by-portion coverage (W1), the building_alternatives list (W3) and the estimate per building (W4) are the 1.4.0 additions.

The conflicting-area rule: docs/plans/R6B_RESULTS_CONNECTION_WORK_ORDER_2026-10-06.md section 6 (lines 229-251; R257, R239); compare_lot_area in result_way_bridge.py (reading O15: agree iff the outline area rounded to the whole square foot equals the recorded figure; benchmark disagrees, 10,388 vs 10,075; no invented tolerance).

The lowest-ratio bound (W2): r6b_lot_coverage.rule.json:44 (corner 100 / interior|through 80), :57-58 (ZR 23-362(b) and 23-363 can lower it; the engine already withholds, result_ways.py:204-234). On the benchmark 0.80 x 10,075 = 8,060 >= building B's plan 6,716.67.
The orchestrator's rulings C1-C18 and the reviews (project-control/reports/M5-T145-G3G4.md); backlog rows DB-210, DB-211, DB-212, DB-196.

The decision layer and emitter as read-only context: result_way_bridge.py:210-216, result_ways.py:116-119/196-254/489-507/619-641, three_way_document.py:97-100/184-216/219-223, geometry.py:53-59.

TASK 1 of 2, reviewed at ONE common head with task 2 and merged as ONE pull request. FOUR parts; up to THREE builders. ORDER: PART A (contract) FIRST, alone; then PARALLEL {PART B server; PART D register checker split + the two DB-211 guards + the DB-211 b fixes (no dependence on B); and, in task 2, PART C the web panel} - three builders on disjoint folders (services/api/app/scenario, services/api/app/rules/review_register, apps/web); then PART D's calc-entry data update + render (after B) and PART E regenerate the document + snapshots + the two server content tests (after B); task 2's web content tests run against PART E's regenerated document. PROOF no two parallel parts share a path: the parallel window is {B, D, C}; B edits services/api/app/scenario/three_answers/* + services/api/tests/scenario/three_answers; D edits services/api/app/rules/review_register + docs/zoning-rule-review + the register test; C (task 2) edits apps/web only - disjoint. PART A and PART E both touch packages/contracts/fixtures/valid/results but never in parallel.

PART A results contract (ADDITIVE 1.4.0): append '1.4.0' to the contract_version enum and add, as OPTIONAL blocks bound by a version allOf (the 1.1.0/1.2.0/1.3.0 pattern; every earlier instance stays valid byte-for-byte): a top-level building_alternatives array - each entry a labelled building with its fill_rule, floor-schedule rows (storey, floor_to_floor_ft, top_ft, plan_area_sqft, floor_area_sqft, running_total_sqft), storey_count, height_ft, total/unused, below_min_base, its way ('settled'|'conditional'|'withheld') with conditions, and its preliminary capacity estimate (quotient_low/high two decimals and unrounded, whole below/above, share_low/high, apartment_size, label exactly 'Not known' or 'Preliminary capacity estimate'); and the by-portion coverage fields (corner/interior ratios, the 100 ft, and the footprint figure only when the areas agree). A withheld result carries NO number (R556/R570). Keep building_option, unit_estimate, floor_stack, floor_by_floor, max_lot_coverage and geometry unchanged in shape. Regenerate packages/contracts/generated/results.ts; add valid fixtures (a 1.4.0 document with building B) and invalid fixtures (a number on a withheld result; a wrong estimate label; a 1.4.0 block declaring 1.3.0).

PART B server: in result_way_bridge.py:210-216 add measure_corner_reach_area(outline, geometry, 100.0). In result_ways.py _coverage_way (:238-254): use compare_lot_area's agree/disagree - DISAGREE -> withhold max_lot_coverage (kind a missing fact; text the law by portion, no figure); AGREE -> call lot_coverage_by_portion and show the footprint. Building (:116-119, :619-641) and three_way_document.py (:97-100, :219-223): call first_building_options; emit building_alternatives with every building that can be worked (building B whenever its plan <= lowest-ratio x recorded area; building A only when the footprint figure is available), each with its capacity estimate from preliminary_apartment_estimate on that building's floor area; the single building_option stays not_available pointing to the list; the standard unit-limit value object (:184-216) stays withheld; name each not-known's kind from the result that failed to supply the input (R650). geometry.py:53-59: draw the footprint and floor plates only when drawable; else carry the withheld reason (M5-T144). Add the DB-212 (d) storey tolerance + test to first_building_options.py. Nothing feasible; the option states what it has not checked.

PART D register: FIRST split review_register_calculations.py behind a compatibility facade (DB-211 c) and add to check_review_register.py the DB-211 (a) guards (bind each six-step verdict to its actual side; require every figure's legal-or-design row) and the DB-211 (b) scenario fixes - no dependence on PART B. THEN, after PART B, update register.json from the engine's new output and render (calc-lot-coverage-by-portion withheld-by-portion, the building-option page showing building B, calc-preliminary-apartment-estimate showing the estimate); no page by hand; no human verdict (R374); state the DB-212 (c) coverage gap (one floor height, 15 ft shop floor not worked).

PART E regenerate: regenerate recorded_215_16_northern_journey.json (now 1.4.0), the site_plan.svg and .dxf snapshots (expected unchanged - geometry unchanged), and update the two server content tests (the journey test and tests/api/test_results_read_api.py) for the additive blocks; run them. Every expected value traces to a named step-p6-worked/real-lot row, never a program run.

THE ORCHESTRATOR'S RULINGS (they govern wherever they differ from the text above). W1: where the recorded lot area and the tax-map outline's area DISAGREE (the existing comparison of reading O15; no tolerance is invented), the footprint in square feet by portion is NOT shown: the outline's area is a drawing measure and is never used in a zoning calculation (work order `docs/plans/R6B_RESULTS_CONNECTION_WORK_ORDER_2026-10-06.md`, section 6; rows R257, R239). The coverage result stays withheld there, kind 'a missing fact about the property' (a survey or deed dimensions would settle it), and its text gives what the law gives by portion without a square-foot figure. Where the two areas agree, the figure is shown. The owner was asked on 2026-10-09 whether to show it instead as conditional on the outline; until an answer, this rule stands. W2: building B is shown where its plan (the allowance divided by its storeys) is at most the LOWEST coverage ratio that can apply to the lot times the RECORDED lot area (benchmark lot: 0.80 x 10,075 = 8,060 sq ft against 6,716.67). The bound is passed to the module as its footprint input and the text says what it is. It applies only where 80 percent is the lowest applicable ratio (the rule file's lower ratios for large lots stay withheld as today). Building B is CONDITIONAL, never settled or confirmed (row R267): on the recorded lot area being confirmed, on the standing conditions every zoning result carries, and on what was not checked. Building A needs the footprint figure: where that is withheld, building A is not listed and is not known (kind: a missing fact about the property). W3: WHICH buildings an option shows is the owner's open decision (backlog row DB-210 b). Until an answer, the document lists EVERY building that can be worked for the lot as a labelled alternative, none marked preferred or default. W4: the estimate is worked for each listed building from that building's own floor area; label exactly as row R543 says. W5: 'the plan fits the coverage' is not 'the building fits the lot'. Each listed building carries, as data and as plain text, what was NOT checked (the rear yard beyond the corner; where the plan sits on the lot; the street wall; parking, loading and bicycle requirements: rows R526, R548). Nothing is called feasible, complies, validated or legally correct. No placement is worked, so no footprint and no floor plate is drawn for the benchmark lot: the geometry block follows every withheld result it draws (task M5-T144). W6: the two tasks (M5-T146 the document, M5-T147 the screen) are built on ONE branch, reviewed at ONE common head and merged as ONE pull request, because the regenerated document changes what the website's tests read. Order: part A (the contract) alone; then part B (server), part D1 (the register checker's split and the two guards of backlog row DB-211) and part C (the website, task M5-T147) side by side on separate folders; then part D2 (the register's data) and part E (the document and snapshots regenerated ONCE); then the website's content tests against the regenerated document. W7: the share range and the apartment size are SHOWN with the values used and called preliminary assumptions. Letting the user CHANGE them on the screen is not in these two tasks unless the existing input path already carries such a value end to end; it is work owed and is recorded in the backlog. W8: a builder who finds that a file outside its part must change STOPS and reports; it does not widen its scope. A legal figure is quoted only from a capture. No human verdict is entered.

SCOPE CORRECTION BY THE ORCHESTRATOR BEFORE PART B STARTS. W9: one new focused module is added to the scope, `services/api/app/scenario/three_answers/first_option_results.py`: `result_ways.py` has 662 lines and must not grow past the size check's lines; the assembling of coverage by portion, the list of worked buildings and their estimates goes into the new module, and the existing files only call it.

SECOND SCOPE CORRECTION BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, AFTER READING PARTS A, B AND E AND BEFORE ANY REVIEW. W10: six more paths are in scope. FOUR were changed by the builder of parts B and E outside its paths and flagged in its report instead of stopping; the orchestrator read each diff and takes them into the task: the bundled copy of the contract schema inside the server (CI requires it byte-identical to the contract; part A had not synced it), `services/api/app/contracts/results_way_rules.py` (the rule of the way layer must also bind version 1.4.0), `services/api/tests/drawings/kit/test_massing.py` (a fixture filter that broke on a document without floor plates) and `services/api/tests/spatial/test_corner_reach_area.py` (the guard of task M5-T145 that nothing imported the measurement "until the wiring step": it now names the two wiring modules). W11 (what the reading of the regenerated benchmark document found, to be corrected before review): (a) the older value state `max_lot_coverage` still gives the old reason and kind (work owed: computing coverage per portion) beside the new block that gives the true one (the two lot areas disagree: a missing fact): two results about one thing must never give different reasons, kinds or resolvers; (b) the older blocks `unit_estimate` and `floor_stack` still say not built yet and not known while the list of buildings carries an estimate and a floor schedule: when the list carries them, the older blocks say where they are given and claim nothing else; (c) the sentence that says why building B fits stands inside the building label: it goes into a field of its own (`fit_note`) and the label stays a short name.

THIRD SCOPE CORRECTION BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, BEFORE ANY REVIEW. W12: the two valid sample documents of part A carry no drawable geometry, so the drawing kit has nothing to snapshot for them; the builder of parts B and E narrowed the drawing tests' fixture list to documents whose geometry is available (`services/api/tests/drawings/kit/kit_support.py`, changed outside its paths and flagged; the orchestrator read it: today it leaves out exactly those two documents). Taken into the task, with a guard so that nothing can drop out of the drawing tests unseen: a test pins the list of left-out documents to exactly those whose geometry is not available, and asserts that the drawing kit answers each of them as unavailable instead of failing (`test_adapter.py`).

FOURTH SCOPE CORRECTION BY THE ORCHESTRATOR, BEFORE ANY REVIEW. W13: (a) the live results route had no prepared outline when the live spatial provider is off, so the two lot areas could not be compared and the first building option was not emitted; the fix lists building B on every path where the allowance is shown (it rests on the recorded lot area and the lowest ratio only) and keeps coverage_by_portion to the case where the areas disagree. One test outside the paths had pinned the old version (`services/api/tests/api/test_results_read_law_examples.py`): read and taken in.
